misconceptions.description: Forgetting the Ad² parallel-axis correction when transferring moment of inertia between axes
misconceptions.trigger: learner sums centroidal I values without adding the Ad² transfer term
misconceptions.feedback: I = I_c + Ad² always. Each piece's centroidal I is about its own centroid; transferring to a common axis requires the Ad² correction.

misconceptions.description: Believing moment of inertia is the same about any parallel axis
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses I_c for an off-center axis without correction
misconceptions.feedback: Parallel axes differ by Ad². The centroidal axis uniquely minimizes I; every other parallel axis is larger.

misconceptions.description: Confusing area moment of inertia with mass moment of inertia because both are labeled I
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses bh³/12 in a τ = Iα equation
misconceptions.feedback: Read the units. Area moment of inertia is m⁴ (statics, bending). Mass moment of inertia is kg·m² (dynamics, rotation). Different quantities; different applications.

misconceptions.description: Replacing a triangular distributed load with a uniform-load equivalent at the midpoint
misconceptions.trigger: learner places a triangular load's equivalent force at L/2
misconceptions.feedback: Equivalent force magnitude is the area under the load curve; equivalent location is the centroid of that area. Triangle: F = w₀L/2 at x = 2L/3 from the zero end, not at midspan.
